title: Escalation Matrix, SLO Experimentation Runway, and Communication Playbook
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working runbook + project plan for a 90-day SLO experimentation runway with an attached escalation matrix and set of communication scripts. The goal: reduce mean user-facing latency regressions and improve error-rate observability by running small, measurable experiments with clear escalation triggers and cross-functional partner involvement.

Scope
- Services in scope: inference-router, cache-layer, prefix-cache, model-serving (g4 pools), edge-gateway.
- Teams: SRE (lead), Serving Runtime, Platform Engineering, Product (Hosted API), Observability, Solutions Eng.
- Not in scope: billing system, internal infra unrelated to request path.

High-level outcomes (90 days)
1) Three live experiments validated with clear metrics and runbooks.
2) Escalation matrix published and exercised in at least one drill.
3) Baseline and post-experiment SLO metrics (latency P95/P99, availability) captured and shared.
4) Communication templates and stakeholder cadence established.

Quick context + assumptions
- We will treat small SLO changes as experiments (canary windows) not policy changes.
- Experiments default to 2-week cycles with a 1-week observation/freeze.
- We assume existing tracing spans and percent-sampled traces available for the services in scope. If not, add instrumentation task to sprint 0.

Roles & responsibilities (working list)
- SRE Lead (Maya Chen): overall runbook owner, coordinates cross-team sprints and drills.
- Service Owner(s) (Serving Runtime: Evan): technical implementation and rollback.
- Platform Eng (Priya): infra provisioning for canary capacity and routing rules.
- Observability (Liam): metric dashboards, alert tuning, experiment dashboards.
- Product / Hosted API PM (Zoe): customer impact prioritization, release comms.
- On-call rotation owners: responsible for responding to escalation matrix triggers.

Escalation matrix (condensed)
- Trigger categories: latency spike, error-rate spike, dependency outage, storage/backplane degradation.
- Initial thresholds (subject to tuning):
  * Latency (P99) > baseline * 1.6 for 10m -> Severity P1 candidate if sustained 30m.
  * Error-rate (5xx) increase > 3x baseline for 5m -> Severity P1 if user-facing.
  * Dependency (cache miss rate increase 20% above baseline) -> P2.
- Immediate actions per trigger:
  1) Automated mitigation: route to fallback model-variant / scale pool (Platform Eng orchestrated).
  2) Pager/Alert: SRE on-call + service owner.
  3) Triage channel: #reliability-incident and a temporary War Room doc auto-created.
  4) If mitigation fails in 30m, escalate to SRE Lead + Eng Manager + Product PM.

Escalation contact matrix (names/emails)
- SRE on-call: pager (rotation) -> see oncall roster link in linked_artifacts.
- Service owner (Serving Runtime): Evan Park (evan@redwood.com).
- Platform lead: Priya Natarajan (priya@redwood.com).
- Observability: Liam O'Connor (liam@redwood.com).
- Product PM: Zoe Ramirez (zoe@redwood.com).

Runway: experiment catalog (prioritized)
Experiment A: Prefix-KV cache warmup window 
- Hypothesis: Pre-warming KV cache for top-50 routes reduces P99 latency by 20% without increasing token-cost.
- Scope: prefix-cache + inference-router.
- Implementation outline: add per-route warmup job and traffic-split (10% canary -> 50% -> rollback/roll-forward).
- Metrics: P95/P99 latency, cache-hit ratio, cost-per-token, user-facing error-rate.
- Rollback plan: automated traffic-shift back to baseline route variant.
- Owner: Serving Runtime + Platform.
- Expected duration: 14 days.

Experiment B: Aggressive batching profile for mid-sized requests
- Hypothesis: Adjusted batching window reduces cost/core-second by 18% while keeping 95th latency within SLO.
- Scope: Batch scheduler, serving runtime kernel parameters.
- Implementation: new batch policy deployed behind feature flag; circuit to revert batching parameters if P95 > SLO + 10%.
- Metrics: throughput (req/s), token-cost, P95 latency, percent of batches hitting timeout.
- Rollback: flip feature flag.
- Owner: Serving Runtime.
- Expected duration: 14 days.

Experiment C: Model variant graceful-fallback chain
- Hypothesis: Multi-variant fallback reduces end-user errors during spike events by 40% and limits cost increase to <5%.
- Scope: router policy, model catalog config, metric-based routing.
- Implementation: create lightweight downgrade variants and add policy to route on health/capacity.
- Metrics: user-error-rate, fallback rate, cost delta, time-to-fallback.
- Rollback: revert routing policy.
- Owner: Platform + Serving Runtime.
- Expected duration: 21 days.

Experiment D (stretch): Canary SLO relaxation for non-critical routes
- Hypothesis: Allowing a small, monitored relaxation for low-risk routes reduces incident volume and operational burden while preserving core-product SLOs.
- Notes: requires strong customer-impact analysis and product signoff.

Experiment governance and acceptance criteria
- Experiment accepted if post-run delta for primary metric meets hypothesis AND secondary metrics (errors, cost) within guardrails.
- If failure mode impacts >1% of active users or an unrecoverable P1 occurs, experiment automatically terminated and postmortem required before re-run.

Instrumentation checklist (Sprint 0)
- Ensure stable P95/P99 dashboards for each service (Observability).
- Add experiment tag to traces to filter canary vs baseline.
- Ensure alerting rules match canary tagging and have suppression window for noisy signals.
- Create automated War Room doc generator (simple template).

Communication plan (stakeholder scripts & cadence)
- Weekly stakeholders sync (30m): SRE lead + experiment owners + product + obs. Send short update: hypothesis, live/finished, primary metric delta, notable incidents, next steps.
- Daily stand while experiment live (15m): only owners + on-call during first 72h.
- Incident comms template (use immediately when P1): 1) Public one-line, 2) What we are doing, 3) ETA for next update, 4) Link to War Room doc.
- Postmortem template: summary, timeline, contributing factors, corrective actions + owners + due dates.

Drill plan (exercise the escalation matrix)
- Week 3: run a planned drill simulating a P2 latency spike during business hours. Objectives: validate paging, war room creation, mitigation automation.
- Participants: SRE on-call, service owner, platform lead, observability engineer, product PM.
- Success criteria: mean time to mitigation < 15m, war room doc created, follow-through on post-drill action items.

Risks & open questions (notes to self)
- Risk: noisy telemetry causing false positives — mitigation: short observation windows and guardrails.
- Risk: customer-facing regressions from batching changes — mitigation: small canary and product opt-in for beta customers.
- Q: Do we have per-route cost attribution at token-level for hosted API? If not, add ticket.
- Q: What is approval process for temporary SLO relaxation? Draft policy needed.

Milestones & rough timeline
- Sprint 0 (2 weeks): instrumentation, dashboards, runbook finalization, drill prep.
- Sprint 1 (weeks 3–4): Experiment A + drill week.
- Sprint 2 (weeks 5–6): Experiment B.
- Sprint 3 (weeks 7–9): Experiment C + product signoff for any relaxations.
- Sprint 4 (week 10–12): consolidate learnings, prepare cross-org recommendations, schedule postmortems + decisions.

Success metrics (how we'll measure program-level success)
- Number of experiments completed to acceptance / started.
- Reduction in P99 latency for targeted routes (absolute ms and percent).
- Reduction in user-facing error rate during spikes.
- Time from trigger to mitigation (MTTM).
- Number of escalations to P1 that are prevented by automated fallback.

Next steps (this week)
- Maya: finalize runbook and share with participating teams (due: Thu).
- Priya: provision canary routing namespace and feature flag pipeline (due: end of sprint 0).
- Liam: create baseline dashboards and add experiment tagging to traces (due: +10 days).
- Evan: draft warmup job prototype and traffic-split plan (due: +10 days).
- Zoe: validate product acceptance criteria and identify low-risk customer cohort for beta (due: +2 weeks).

Appendix (links + templates)
- War Room doc template: short description, timeline, mitigation steps, tech contacts, postmortem link.
- Incident comms snippets: short one-liners + status update bullets.
- Slack channel list + pager rotation link (see linked_artifacts).

Notes / scratchpad (informal)
- If we can tag traces at router-level, it will make experiment attribution much clearer.
- Consider adding a lightweight canary UI in console showing active experiments and their primary metric deltas (future wishlist).
- TODO: schedule a 30-minute pre-mortem discussion with product and solutions eng before each experiment launch.

End of doc.
